headline: Multi-omic profiling maps conserved remodeling programs across tissue aging and fibrosis
label: Single Cell Tissue Remodeling Atlases
summary: Recent cross-species and tissue atlases link single-cell states to aging, fibrosis, and niche remodeling across several organs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of single-cell and integrated transcriptomic or proteomic profiling to resolve cell-state programs in remodeling tissues. Several items pair atlases with network or machine-learning prioritization: a cross-species ovarian atlas nominates Stat3 and Max in aging, WGCNA and STEM applied to satellite cell time-series nominate THBS1 and LAMA5 for stemness, and an ML and spatial workflow identifies ferro-aging biomarkers in ulcerative colitis. Other studies localize regulators to specific stromal or immune compartments, including RUNX1 in POSTN+ fibroblasts during skin fibrosis, LTBP4-driven fibroblast reprogramming in ossifying ligamentum flavum, and an INHBA-associated macrophage-MuSC axis in aged human muscle. The contribution is the framing of these programs as candidate regulators spanning aging, fibrosis, and vascular remodeling, though most findings remain nominations requiring experimental validation.
